hero.title: From download to live captions in four steps.
hero.summary: No plugin for your viewers, no re-streaming your gameplay to the cloud — just your microphone audio, translated in real time.

steps.title: Download the desktop app
steps.body: Grab the Strovak desktop app for Windows (Mac/Linux support is on the roadmap). It runs alongside OBS or your streaming software of choice.

steps.title: Pair it with a code
steps.body: Your dashboard shows a one-time 6-digit code. Type it into the app once — it stays paired for 30 days, no re-entering it every stream.

steps.title: Add the overlay to OBS
steps.body: Copy your overlay URL from the Captions page and add it as a Browser Source in OBS. It shows live translated captions on top of your scene.

steps.title: Go live like you always do
steps.body: Stream to Twitch, Kick or YouTube as usual. The app sends only your mic audio to the cloud; everything else stays on your machine.

howItWorks.privacyNote: Your video, gameplay, and scene never leave your PC — only a small encrypted audio stream (roughly 50–128 Kbps) goes to the cloud for captioning and translation.

faq.question: Does my video ever get uploaded?
faq.answer: No. The desktop app only captures microphone audio. Your video is encoded and sent by your own streaming software, exactly like today — Strovak never receives it.

faq.question: Do I need OBS specifically?
faq.answer: The overlay works as a browser source in any software that supports one (OBS, Streamlabs, vMix, etc). OBS is just the most common setup, so our instructions use it as the example.

faq.question: What happens when I run out of monthly hours?
faq.answer: Captioning pauses until the next billing period or until you upgrade — see the Pricing page for each plan's included hours and overage rate.

faq.question: Can I use my own cloned voice for dubbing?
faq.answer: Yes, on the Pro and Streamer plans. You record a short consented sample in the dashboard's Voice cloning studio, and it's reviewed before going live.

faq.question: Which platforms can I stream to?
faq.answer: Twitch, YouTube and Kick are supported today, with per-platform captioning or dubbed-channel options — see the Distribution page in your dashboard.

pages.title: Terms of Service
pages.summary: The rules for using Strovak, including account access, acceptable use, subscriptions and service limits.

sections.title: Using Strovak
sections.body: Strovak is operated from Lithuania. You may use Strovak to capture audio, generate live captions, translate speech and route supported streaming outputs according to your plan. You are responsible for the content you stream and for keeping your account credentials secure.

sections.title: Accounts and plans
sections.body: Plan limits, billing periods, feature access and fair-use rules are shown in the dashboard and may change when your subscription changes. Paid features must be used only with a valid payment method or active entitlement.

sections.title: Acceptable use
sections.body: Do not use the service to violate platform rules, impersonate others, distribute illegal content, bypass usage limits or process audio without the rights and consents required for your stream, event or organization.

sections.title: Service changes
sections.body: Real-time services depend on third-party providers, network conditions and platform APIs. We may update providers, limits, routes and safety controls to keep the service reliable and compliant.

sections.title: Contact
sections.body: Questions about these terms can be sent to legal@strovak.com.

pages.title: Privacy Policy
pages.summary: How Strovak handles account data, operational logs and the audio-only cloud pipeline used for live translation.

sections.title: What we process
sections.body: We process account information, authentication events, plan and usage records, integration status, support messages and the audio data needed to provide live captions and translations. Video remains local and is not uploaded by the Phase 1 pipeline.

sections.title: Why we process it
sections.body: Data is used to provide the service, secure accounts, enforce plan limits, diagnose incidents, improve reliability, process payments and meet legal obligations. Provider API keys and stream keys are treated as secrets.

sections.title: Retention and deletion
sections.body: Operational records are kept only as long as needed for service, security, billing or legal reasons. To request deletion of your account and related records, contact legal@strovak.com.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: Depending on your location, you may request access, correction, deletion, objection, restriction or portability for personal data. KVKK and GDPR-style requests should be sent to legal@strovak.com.

pages.title: KVKK Disclosure Notice
pages.summary: A KVKK-focused notice for users in Turkey, covering data controller duties, processing purposes and data subject rights.

sections.title: Data controller and scope
sections.body: This notice explains how personal data may be processed for Strovak accounts, dashboard access, live audio translation, billing, security logging and support. Strovak is operated from Lithuania; formal company registration details will be published on this page once registration is complete. Until then, KVKK inquiries should be sent to legal@strovak.com.

sections.title: Processing purposes
sections.body: Personal data may be processed to create accounts, verify users, provide live caption and translation services, manage subscriptions, protect infrastructure, respond to support requests and comply with applicable law.

sections.title: Transfers and recipients
sections.body: Data may be shared with hosting, payment, email, analytics, speech-to-text, translation, text-to-speech and streaming integration providers only as needed to deliver the service. As Strovak operates from within the EU/EEA, cross-border transfers to Turkey and back follow the safeguards required under both KVKK and GDPR.

sections.title: KVKK rights
sections.body: Users may request information about processing, correction, deletion, anonymization, transfer recipients, objection to adverse results and compensation for unlawful processing where applicable under KVKK Article 11. Send requests to legal@strovak.com; we aim to respond within 30 days as required by KVKK.

sections.title: Essential storage
sections.body: The dashboard may use cookies, local storage or similar technologies to keep users signed in, remember language and interface preferences, protect sessions and route authenticated API requests.

sections.title: Analytics and diagnostics
sections.body: If analytics or diagnostics are enabled, they should be configured to measure reliability, page health and product usage without collecting unnecessary personal data. Optional analytics should follow the consent mode chosen for the deployment.

sections.title: Third-party tools
sections.body: Payment, support, email, streaming platform and infrastructure tools may set their own cookies or identifiers when their services are used. Their notices should be linked from the production privacy center when enabled.

sections.title: Managing choices
sections.body: Browser settings can block or delete cookies, but essential authentication and security storage may be required for the dashboard, admin console and overlay builder to work correctly. Questions about this policy can be sent to legal@strovak.com.

sections.title: Roles
sections.body: For customer-controlled streams and events, the customer may act as data controller and Strovak may act as data processor for service data processed on the customer's instructions.

sections.title: Processor commitments
sections.body: Processor commitments cover confidentiality, security measures, subprocessors, incident notice, deletion or return of data, audit support and assistance with data subject requests. Signed DPA requests can be sent to legal@strovak.com.

sections.title: Subprocessors
sections.body: Speech, translation, email, payment, hosting, logging and support providers may be subprocessors when enabled. Strovak publishes the current subprocessor list and notice process on request.

sections.title: Security measures

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.subtitle: Provider API keys entered here go live immediately, without a restart. Values are always masked: only the start and end are readable.

secrets.maskNote: Values are masked server-side: the API returns only the first and last characters of each secret (for example sk_l...3456). The full value never leaves the server.
secrets.note: Keys resolve at call time, so a key saved here activates its provider on the next request. In production set providers.mock_fallback to false under Service routing so missing keys fail loudly instead of producing mock output.

sttServers.title: STT Servers
sttServers.subtitle: Add a GPU VPS/VDS from any provider once you have paying customers to justify the cost. The backend generates an SSH keypair, installs the self-hosted faster-whisper service over SSH, and reports back when it's ready.
sttServers.publicEndpointHint: Only needed if the reachable STT port differs from the SSH port's host — e.g. on Vast.ai the SSH port and the STT service port are usually mapped to two different external ports; check the instance's port list and enter the STT one here.
sttServers.publicKeyIntro: Add this public key to the server. On Vast.ai: add it under Account > SSH Keys BEFORE creating the instance (existing instances don't pick up new account keys — use the instance's own SSH-key panel instead). On a regular VPS: pass it at creation time or paste it into authorized_keys. Then click Install.
sttServers.confirmDelete: Remove this server record? This does not touch the remote machine, only StreamDubber's record of it.
